The excess is 18.16 km and 50.44% of the optimal route. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test are satisfied — the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms — so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-04 cannot be invoked: the chat log EV-CHAT-00105 carries only three messages — two rider queries about the route and the driver's 'reaching soon' — with no rider instruction to detour, and every waypoint_hint is null. There is no rider-requested detour to exclude from the excess.

No endpoint was amended: trip_record.pickup_amended_at and trip_record.dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not re-baseline the optimal route against amended endpoints.

This is not a pooled trip: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 does not substitute a matched-itinerary baseline and the 36.0 km optimal route stands as the comparison figure.

The fare model is METERED on EV-FARE-00105, so POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x surge 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36. charged_total is 65.13. Refund = 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, which rounds up to SGD 21.80.

I disclose that EV-DPROF-00105 is IMPAIRED — weight 0.75, issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT — and the finding survives the discount because 4 clears the threshold of 3 even on a lagged snapshot. Under POL-RD-06(b) a deviation that is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total: 65.13, set beside the POL-RD-02 figure of 21.80, with no ERP, toll or surcharge pass-through lines to carve out.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: EV-GPS-00105 has 100% coverage, 427 fixes at a 10 second interval, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not met and the deviation may be established on the trace alone without independent corroboration.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is met: the trip identifier matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and the trace-measured excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold by a wide margin. The burden shifts to the driver, who has pointed to no artifact and no exculpatory clause.

There are no pass-through lines to settle separately under POL-RD-09: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0 and airport_surcharge is 0.0, which is correct because the Changi surcharge applies only to trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this one terminates there. Nothing therefore reduces or inflates the refund owed to the rider.

The driver's account attributes the longer route to heavy traffic on the PIE — an invocation of the POL-RD-03 exoneration — and the pool contains no traffic_advisory to support it: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and its only issue is the blocking MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-10(5) makes precisely this combination a mandatory escalation trigger: an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact missing from the pool, its own worked example being 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory'. The disputed $65.13 must therefore be held rather than refunded, pending a human who can obtain the LTA advisory for the 14:26-15:44 window on 15 July 2026, which is the outcome that protects the driver from a final refund on an incomplete record.

Even if the deviation is taken as established, the remedy is fixed by POL-RD-02 and is arithmetic, not the whole fare the rider demands. On fare_model METERED with the surge multiplier read from EV-FARE-00105 (surge_multiplier 1.0), the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 43.36, so the refund is 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80. That is a partial refund; the rider's demand for the entire fare refunded, and his characterisation of the trip, do not control the outcome under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02.

The only artifact that could lift the remedy above the POL-RD-02 partial to a FULL_REFUND is the driver profile, and that artifact is impaired. ruling.explanation: To the rider: your claim is upheld in full. Under POL-RD-01 the GPS trace governs, and EV-GPS-00105 records 54.16 km against the platform's optimal 36.0 km on EV-TRIP-00105 — an excess of 18.16 km, 50.44% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED, and the same excess also clears both materiality thresholds (greater than 50% and greater than 8.0 km), so it is MATERIAL. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 100% coverage, 427 fixes at a 10-second interval, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so no independent corroboration is required and the deviation stands on the trace alone. No exculpatory clause applies — there is no rider-requested detour in the chat (POL-RD-04), no endpoint amendment (POL-RD-05), no pooled itinerary (POL-RD-12) and no traffic advisory (POL-RD-03). To the driver: your account that traffic was heavy is considered, but a bare statement is not a traffic_advisory, and an assertion that cites no evidence does not discharge your burden under POL-RD-08; POL-RD-03 requires an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, and EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is absent from the record at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no exoneration arises. Your request that the case escalate under POL-RD-10(5) is rejected: that trigger requires an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and your account cited none — a general 'traffic was bad' assertion is dealt with by POL-RD-08 as a failure of proof, not as a gap in the record, and the trace is in any event unimpaired. On the remedy: the fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 fixes the base figure — recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x surge 1.0 (read from EV-FARE-00105) + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36, giving 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80. That partial is then uplifted. Your driver-profile point is well taken but does not defeat the pattern: EV-DPROF-00105 is impaired at weight 0.75 with issue STALE_SNAPSHOT, yet deviation_flags_90d is 4 against a threshold of 3, so the POL-RD-06 pattern finding survives the discount; the impairment only caps confidence in this ruling at 0.75, which remains above the 0.70 floor. Because the deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total rather than the POL-RD-02 partial. Stating both figures side by side as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 figure = SGD 21.80; uplifted figure under POL-RD-06(b) = SGD 65.13. Nothing is carved out of the uplift, because there are no pass-through lines: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.0 and the airport surcharge is 0.0 — and that zero surcharge is correct, since the Changi surcharge applies only to trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this trip terminates there, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction arises. The full contested amount of SGD 65.13 is therefore refunded to the rider, and the repeat-pattern finding additionally produces the POL-RD-06(c) referral recorded above.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 4 (threshold 3), so a repeat-deviation pattern is established and the driver is referred to driver-conduct review; this referral does not delay or displace the monetary ruling.
